title: Wither-mark
sentences: A wither-mark is a withered stump that stands on a gardener's lot border for every large past sell in their wallet's history.
Wither-marks are permanent and cannot be removed or stolen, because history is landscape in Pons Garden.
A sell counts as a wither-mark when it was a fifth or more of the wallet's holdings at the time.

title: Conviction tree
sentences: The conviction tree is the centrepiece tree in the corner of a wallet-linked lot and it grows with the time the wallet has held.
The conviction tree passes through five stages named seedling, sapling, mature, flowering and fruiting.
The conviction tree cannot be stolen or removed.

title: Fence
sentences: A fence is a defense bought with Sap that closes a lot's gate so thieves cannot simply walk in.
A closed gate takes three loud hits to break, and each hit is announced on the notice board.
A broken gate can be repaired with Sap from the shop.

title: Gnome sentry
sentences: A gnome sentry is a defense that patrols a gardener's lot in a slow circle.
The gnome tags any thief who comes within reach, which returns the plant and pays the owner a bounty.
A gnome can wear a wizard hat, a crown or a propeller bought as decor.

title: Sprinkler turret
sentences: A sprinkler turret is a defense that slows anyone carrying a plant through the lot.
The sprinkler stands in the corner of the lot and sprays while it works.

title: Plot lock
sentences: A plot lock is a consumable defense that makes one plot immune to theft for a whole day.
A locked plot shows a small padlock beside the plant.

title: Scarecrow
sentences: A scarecrow is a decoy that looks exactly like a gnome sentry to every other gardener and does nothing at all.
A scarecrow costs less than a gnome and is meant to make thieves hesitate.

title: Mud patch
sentences: A mud patch is a defense that slows anyone who is not the owner while they are inside the lot.
A lot with a mud patch shows churned brown soil inside its fence.

title: Gate bell
sentences: A gate bell is a defense that tells the owner the moment anyone steps into their garden.
The gate bell rings for the owner wherever they are in the village.

title: Thief
sentences: A thief is any gardener who uproots a plant from another gardener's lot and carries it away.
A thief moves more slowly while carrying a plant and drops it at once if the owner or a gnome touches them.
A thief who is tagged buys the next round, according to Bram the Barkeep.
A gardener who was robbed can post a bounty on the thief for an hour.

title: Tag
sentences: To tag a thief, the owner or the owner's gnome touches the thief while they are carrying a plant.
A tag returns the plant to its plot at once and pays the owner a bounty of Sap.
A tag also cancels an uprooting that is still in progress.

title: Carrying
sentences: Carrying is the state of a thief holding an uprooted plant above their head while running home.
A carrying thief moves at seven tenths of normal speed and slower still through a sprinkler or mud.
The carried plant is replanted when the thief reaches their own lot.

title: Hat
sentences: A gardener may wear a straw hat, a cap, a top hat or a bandana, and may change their shirt colour for a little Sap.
Hats are bought once with Sap and kept forever in the wardrobe.
Everyone in the village sees a gardener's hat and shirt.

title: Decor
sentences: Decor is bought with Sap and changes how a lot looks without changing how it plays.
A lot's fence can be wood, a stone wall with an iron gate, or a hedge.
Gate lanterns light up at night, a nameplate stands by the gate, and a cobbled path can ring the plots.

title: Trophies
sentences: Trophies are kept on the notice board for the week's most steals, most tags and biggest heist.
Trophies reset every Monday so a new gardener can take the board.

title: Nickname
sentences: A gardener can give any of their plants a nickname of up to fourteen letters.
A nickname travels with the plant when it is stolen and appears in the village feed.
